transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Claire Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Gomez (Maverick Head of Platform), Ethan Liu (Maverick SRE), Priya Das (Maverick Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick ops handshake to confirm numbers for the renewal + expansion. High-level alignment on dedicated capacity plus burst pool. Security questions noted; legal loop after benchmarks.

[00:00] Claire Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intro - I'm Claire, AE at Redwood. Samir here is our SE who will lead the benchmark and perf questions. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Nina Gomez: Good, thanks. Busy week but we're ready to move this forward.
[00:12] Ethan Liu: Yeah, hi. Wanted to make sure we get the right numbers because our Q4 ramp is, uh, pretty sharp.
[00:17] Claire Morales: Totally. Goal for today is to align on the capacity bump, talk EU region timing, and lock down action items so procurement can start the internal flow.
[00:27] Priya Das: From procurement side I just need timelines and the final T&Cs. We don't need the full contract today but we need to know whether this is a 12- or 24- month commit and what the uplift looks like.
[00:38] Samir Patel: Cool. I put together a couple capacity options — small bump (30% reserved), mid (60% reserved + 20% burst), and large (90% reserved). Each has different unit costs and latency guarantees.
[00:49] Nina Gomez: Can you repeat the burst idea? We've used burst pools before but want to know if the failover is seamless.
[00:54] Samir Patel: Yeah so burst is a shared capacity pool that Redwood Dedicated can add on top of reserved. If your traffic spikes above reserved, requests route into burst. There's a small extra per-token premium for burst. On failover, we have automatic routing to a compatible model variant. Sometimes transcript shows Redwood dedicote—sorry, that's me reading the notes—should be Redwood Dedicated.
[01:20] Ethan Liu: Are there cold-starts on the burst nodes or is the cache warmed?
[01:24] Samir Patel: Good question. We do some proactive KV cache warming for predictable endpoints if you share the prefix patterns. For unknown spikes there can be a short ramp (~200-800ms) while caches fill and kernels JIT. That is, worst-case small tail latency.
[01:38] Nina Gomez: That tail concerns us. Our p99 SLA needs to stay under 600ms for the user-facing endpoints. Can we commit to that on the mid option?
[01:45] Samir Patel: For mid option, with 60% reserved and a tuned batching profile, we think p99 at typical traffic will be around 450-500ms. For very large spikes you might hit the >600ms window for a few minutes unless you size reserved higher.
[01:58] Claire Morales: Tradeoff is cost vs latency. We priced mid to keep the monthly commitment reasonable while absorbing short spikes.
[02:05] Priya Das: On pricing, can you show the uplift per region? EU is more expensive for us because of egress.
[02:11] Claire Morales: Yes. We have a regional multiplier for EU due to infra and data residency. I'll include a table in the updated quote. Also note any data transfer egress will be itemized; we can push some traffic through edge to reduce egress but depends on your architecture.
[02:24] Nina Gomez: Speaking of residency — we need to know if Redwood Private (VPC) is required or if we can use Hosted with regional tenancy. We're trying to avoid a full Private deployment if possible.
[02:34] Samir Patel: Hosted with customer-region tenancy can meet many needs; Private/VPC gives you isolated control plane and KMS integration. For regulated data, Private is recommended. Otherwise hosted with strict retention rules could be fine.
[02:46] Ethan Liu: Our security checklist: SOC2 report, audit logs retention for 13 months, KMS integration, SSO (SAML). Are those all in the standard enterprise pack?
[02:55] Claire Morales: Yes, SOC2 and SAML/SSO and audit logs are part of the enterprise offering. KMS integration for bring-your-own-key is available for Private deployments; for hosted we can do envelope encryption and manage keys if required. We noted security packet — we'll share that after this call.
[03:11] Priya Das: Important: procurement wants the KMS option priced. If Private costs are significantly higher, we need to know the delta.
[03:17] Claire Morales: Absolutely. I'll include a separate line item for Private + KMS in the quote.
[03:21] Nina Gomez: On benchmarks — we want to run a 2-hour synthetic run that simulates our burst profile. Can you provision a test harness?
[03:28] Samir Patel: We can. I propose a 2-hour block on Dedicated with a replica of your top-5 endpoints, then we capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput. We'll need the dataset and request distribution.
[03:36] Ethan Liu: I can provide token distribution and latency targets, plus a recording of traffic curve. We might need a couple of warm-up runs.
[03:42] Samir Patel: Warm-ups are fine. Also: please note some model names might be transcribed weirdly in our notes; if you see Redwood verfy or verRedwood, it's just the speech-to-text.
[03:52] Nina Gomez: Haha ok, good to know.
[03:55] Claire Morales: On contract term — we often discount at commit levels: 12 months baseline, 18 months small additional discount, 24 months largest. But customers often prefer 12 months with a built-in option to convert to longer terms after the first quarter.
[04:10] Priya Das: Procurement prefers clear renewal triggers. If we sign 12 months with a capacity ramp schedule, when does the price lock in?
[04:16] Claire Morales: Price lock occurs at signature for the committed reserved capacity. Burst pricing and any new regions would be added as add-ons with the rates in the quote. We can include an escalation clause for large scale increases.
[04:28] Ethan Liu: Is there a minimum notice for adding EU capacity?
[04:31] Samir Patel: Provisioning EU Dedicated capacity typical lead time is 8-12 business days for moderate sizes; for very large pools maybe longer. For Hosted, region onboarding can be faster, but if you want isolated nodes in EU as Dedicated we need that 8-12 day window.
[04:44] Nina Gomez: That lines up with our planned October traffic increase. If we sign end of July we'd want EU capacity live by mid-September. Is that feasible?
[04:51] Samir Patel: Feasible if we lock sizes this week — that gives us the provisioning runway.
[04:56] Claire Morales: Action: Claire will update quote with mid-option and large-option, include EU uplift and private/KMS delta. Samir will own the benchmark plan. Nina and Ethan to share traffic pattern artifacts. Priya to share procurement calendar.
[05:10] Priya Das: From internal procurement notes we also need standard indemnities and a data processing addendum — can you confirm Redwood has a DPA?
[05:17] Claire Morales: Yes, we have a DPA and can provide the template. Legal tends to look at the DPA and data residency clauses.
[05:22] Ethan Liu: Any concerns about model quantization or accuracy loss if we use lower precision to save cost? We run a lot of semantic search and chat — small regressions matter.
[05:30] Samir Patel: Good point. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles. For production customer-facing endpoints we recommend validation via eval suite. If accuracy delta is unacceptable, we avoid aggressive quantization. We can run a controlled eval as part of the benchmark.
[05:44] Nina Gomez: Can we get a sample eval harness from you?
[05:47] Samir Patel: Yep, I'll drop the evaluation scripts and example prompts.
[05:50] Claire Morales: Any vendor comparison questions?
[05:52] Nina Gomez: We're also talking to GigaServe — their price is lower for pure hosted, but they don't offer the same private KMS integration. That's a factor.
[05:59] Priya Das: And CloudNimble has an aggressive p99 SLA claim but their observability is weaker which makes our ops team nervous.
[06:06] Claire Morales: Good context. We'll make sure the quote highlights the SLA, observability features, and the fallbacks we provide (model variants/region failover).
[06:14] Ethan Liu: One last technical — how does token accounting work for caching? Does prefix cache reduce billed tokens?
[06:20] Samir Patel: We bill based on tokens generated and consumed. Prefix/KV caching reduces compute because the model can skip repeated context, but tokens sent still count if they cross the wire. For some flows we can do server-side caching to reduce billable tokens; we can share patterns.
[06:35] Nina Gomez: That might help our cost model. Can you show examples in the quote?
[06:39] Claire Morales: Will do.
[06:41] [09:12] (note: timestamps in segments occasionally jump — automated transcript artifact)
[06:45] Samir Patel: For the benchmark success criteria I propose: p95 < 400ms for core endpoints, p99 < 600ms, throughput >= X rps per node (we'll compute X after we see your traffic profile). Also, accuracy regression < 0.5% on your eval set.
[06:58] Nina Gomez: Sounds reasonable. We'll provide the eval set.
[07:01] Claire Morales: Anything else on the contract terms?
[07:04] Priya Das: We need cancellation terms spelled out and a table for prorated refunds if we reduce reserved mid-term. Also an SLA credit schedule.
[07:13] Claire Morales: We can include prorated adjustments and a clear SLA credit table. Legal usually takes those and tweaks.
[07:19] Ethan Liu: For quick wins, can we pilot the mid option for 60 days? A short pilot might reduce procurement friction.
[07:26] Claire Morales: We can do a pilot, typically that goes through a pilot addendum with defined metrics and a short commit. But procurement likes clarity on the pilot scope and what converts to production.
[07:36] Priya Das: If pilot is 60 days, procurement needs conversion terms and a not-to-exceed on spending.
[07:42] Claire Morales: Noted. Include that in the quote as Pilot Addendum A.
[07:46] Nina Gomez: Ok, final recap?
[07:48] Claire Morales: Recap: 1) Claire to send updated quote with reserved+burst options, EU uplift, private/KMS delta, pilot addendum by 2026-07-27. 2) Samir to send benchmark plan and evaluation scripts by 2026-07-24 and schedule a 2-hour run with Ethan/Nina for 2026-07-29. 3) Nina/Ethan to provide traffic profile and eval set by 2026-07-25. 4) Priya to share procurement timeline by 2026-07-30.
[08:10] Priya Das: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to review quote and get procurement started.
[08:14] Claire Morales: Great, thanks. I'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window.
[08:20] (call ends)

Notes: occasional ASR errors in product names and acronyms (e.g., V-P-C transcribed as VPC, kv cash for KV cache). Transcript intentionally retains spoken hesitations and clarifications.
